saint-charbel-places-lebanon.saint-charb: Saint Charbel's Lebanon: Bekaa Kafra, Mayfouq & Annaya

Saint Charbel's whole life fits on a small map of the Lebanese mountains. He was born in Bekaa Kafra, widely known as the country's highest village; he became a monk at Mayfouq; and he lived, died, and lies entombed at Annaya. Visiting the three in order is walking his story from beginning to end - and the new Darb Mar Charbel trail now ties them together on foot.

As a boy he tended the family's flock on these slopes, and he found a secluded cave where he would slip away to pray for hours - the spot villagers still know as the

still stands: after his death and the spread of devotion, the Lebanese Maronite Order acquired the family home, and monks care for it today as a small shrine and museum of his childhood world - plain rooms, simple tools, nothing grand, which is exactly what moves the pilgrims who come.
Bekaa Kafra is roughly 120 kilometers from Beirut, about two hours by car into the high mountains. Give it a full day and pair it with Bsharri, the Cedars, and the

saint-charbel-places-lebanon.mayfouq-whe: Mayfouq: Where He Became a Monk (1851-1853)
In 1851, at twenty-three, Youssef left his village and walked south to the
Monastery of Our Lady of Mayfouq
, the novitiate of the Lebanese Maronite Order. There he received the habit and took the name

, after an early martyr of the Church of Antioch - the name the whole world now knows him by. Mayfouq was his school of monastic beginnings: prayer, work, fasting, and obedience, the pattern he would keep for the rest of his life.
Mayfouq matters to pilgrims for a second reason: it is the far end of the first open section of the
, which runs from Annaya to Mayfouq. Walking that section, you cross in a day the same ground the young novice crossed for good in 1851.
saint-charbel-places-lebanon.annaya-wher: Annaya: Where He Lived, Died, and Lies Entombed (1853-1898)
In 1853 Brother Charbel moved to the
Monastery of Saint Maron in Annaya
, in the Jbeil district of Mount Lebanon, and made his perpetual vows. He was ordained a priest in 1859. After more than two decades of monastic life he received permission in 1875 to withdraw to the
hermitage of Saints Peter and Paul
on the hill above the monastery - and there he spent his final twenty-three years in silence, prayer, and penance, until his death on
Annaya is the destination of the pilgrimage: the tomb in the great church, the hermitage above, the holy oil, daily Mass, and the crowds of the
Pope Leo XIV came as a pilgrim on December 1, 2025
- the first pope ever to pray at the tomb. Our
covers the drive, the order of what to see, and the practical details.
saint-charbel-places-lebanon.how-the-thr: The geography tells the theology. Bekaa Kafra is the root: a mountain childhood of work and prayer. Mayfouq is the calling: the doorway into religious life. Annaya is the gift complete: forty-five years of monastic fidelity, twenty-three of them in a hermit's cell. Pilgrims who can only manage one stop choose Annaya, because the tomb is there. Pilgrims with two or three days add Bekaa Kafra and the north, and walk the trail's first open section between Annaya and Mayfouq.
